steps: In CSS, every HTML element is treated as a rectangular box. The CSS box model describes the parts of this box and how they are arranged.
The content is the text, image, or other material inside the element.
Padding is the space between the content and the border. It surrounds the content, inside the border.
The border surrounds both the content and the padding.
Margin is the transparent space outside the border. It separates the element from neighbouring elements.
Thus, from the inside out, the order is: content, padding, border, and margin.
Example: `p { margin: 10px; border: 1px solid black; padding: 5px; }` adds padding around the paragraph content, a border around the padding, and margin outside the border.
items.finalAnswer: The CSS box model shows how content, padding, border, and margin fit together: padding surrounds content, the border surrounds the padding, and margin lies outside the border.

steps: Create a table in HTML and apply CSS rules to its table, header cells, and data cells.

The `border` property adds lines around the cells. `border-collapse: collapse` combines adjoining borders into single lines. `padding` adds space inside each cell, `text-align` aligns the cell text, and `background-color` colours the heading cells.
items.finalAnswer: A table can be styled with CSS properties such as `border`, `border-collapse`, `padding`, `text-align`, and `background-color`.

steps: A CSS selector selects the HTML element or elements to which a CSS rule is applied.
Element selector: selects all elements with a specified tag name. Example: `p { color: blue; }` selects all paragraphs.
ID selector: selects the element with a specified `id`. It is written with `#`. Example: `#title { color: red; }` selects the element with `id="title"`.
Class selector: selects all elements with a specified class. It is written with a dot (`.`). Example: `.note { background-color: yellow; }` selects elements with `class="note"`.
Universal selector: selects all elements. It is written as `*`. Example: `* { font-family: Arial; }`.
Grouping selector: applies the same declarations to more than one selector. Example: `h1, h2 { color: green; }` selects all `h1` and `h2` elements.
Descendant selector: selects an element inside another specified element. Example: `div p { color: purple; }` selects paragraphs inside a `div` element.
items.finalAnswer: CSS selectors include element, ID, class, universal, grouping, and descendant selectors; each selects elements for CSS styling.

steps: A responsive web page adjusts its layout to suit different screen sizes, such as mobile phones, tablets, and computers.
Use the viewport meta tag so the page uses the device's screen width: `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">`.
Use flexible widths instead of fixed widths where possible. Example: `img { max-width: 100%; height: auto; }` makes an image shrink to fit its container while keeping its proportions.
Use a media query to apply different CSS rules at different screen widths. Example:
The rule inside `@media (max-width: 600px)` applies when the screen width is 600 pixels or less. It reduces the text size and lets the container use the full screen width.
Flexible images and widths, together with media queries, help a page display properly on different devices.
items.finalAnswer: A responsive page uses the viewport meta tag, flexible sizes, and media queries to adapt its layout to different screen widths.

steps: A CSS transition changes a property smoothly from one value to another over a specified time, usually when an element's state changes.
The `transition` property specifies which property changes and how long the change takes. Here, the button's background changes smoothly from blue to red over one second when the pointer is over it.
A CSS animation can change styles through a sequence of keyframes.
`@keyframes` defines the style changes in the animation. `animation-name` selects the keyframes to use, and `animation-duration` sets how long the animation takes.
items.finalAnswer: Transitions smoothly change CSS properties between states, while animations use `@keyframes` and animation properties to change styles over time.
